Here’s some insight on how publishing deals and advances work, at least for regular authors (might be different for celebrities, not sure):

Advances are based on projected sales. They’re an advance of money that the publisher projects will be made back in sales. Any money made beyond the advance is paid as royalties, of which the author gets a percentage.

Advances are split into three payments: one when you sign the deal, one after you’ve finished edits with your editor and submitted the completed manuscript, and one when the book comes out.

Most authors never earn out their advances. Most never make it to the point of earning royalties.

Did “Becoming” sell 10 million copies in 5-6 months? No way. Her advance was the publisher’s guess at how much money they could make from book sales. Did she earn back her advance in 5-6 months?
